title: Bodybuilder Roasts AI Generated Program
summary: NH critiques a 7-day bro split generated by ChatGPT. The AI stacks redundant exercises back to back, pairs unrelated muscles, adds an abs-and-cardio day, places rest days badly and gives no sets or reps. When asked, it repeats rep-range myths and 'keep the muscles guessing'; NH concludes his job is safe.
claims: NH says he works in AI, which makes him skeptical of chatbot intelligence
Three chest presses plus cable flies in a row is a lot; close-grip bench after triceps isolation is a redundant compound that mirrors the bench
Bro splits are the worst training template; training a muscle once a week forces piling many exercises into one session
If you do two similar back exercises in a day (pull-ups and pulldowns), separate them rather than doing them back to back
You can open a back and biceps day with a heavy row/pull instead for more stimulus
Back and biceps have little synergy; chest and triceps do; pulling does not blow up your arms
Chin-ups would suit a back and biceps day better than pull-ups
Shoulders and legs do not go well together; front raises are redundant after shoulder presses
Supersets are one of the best things for bodybuilding, ignored by popular bro splits
An abs and cardio day is a filler day; spread ab exercises across the week to recover and grow
Push-ups and dips on day 7 followed by heavy chest and triceps on day 1 ignores that the week repeats
'6-8 reps for strength, 8-12 for size, 12+ for endurance' is a popular myth; hypertrophy can use 6-10, 8-12 or 10-15 depending on preference and what you need to progress
'Keep the muscles guessing' is bro science
